item.title: Boy Golden Finds the Best Things in Life
item.description: Boy Golden has given us a soundtrack for good times, which is an achievement that, in our current world, feels nothing short of miraculous.

item.title: Melissa Aldana Creates Ideal Latin American Balladry
item.description: The overall sensation of Melissa Alada's Filin is not just beauty but distillation. The songs, even those without sung lyrics, get definitive interpretations.

item.title: Daphni Lights Up the Dancefloor with Sparkling Beats
item.description: Daphni's Butterfly is made to get you moving, designed for the club, but it will sound equally as massive in the living room discos.

item.title: My Most Anticipated Films of 2026
item.description: As surely as "Dumpuary January" follows the fall awards season, a new year brings a slew of anticipated films. If the industry is in trouble, nobody has told these directors.

item.title: 10 Should-Be-Classic Anxious Love Songs
item.description: Anxious love songs typically involve conflict—around unrequited passion, cheating, or loss—where the singer often feels something unresolved.

item.title: Scott McCloud Powerfully Reflects on the Past
item.description: Girls Against Boys singer Scott McCloud shows a quieter, more reflective side in this addictive collection of solo tracks, Forever.

item.title: Nick Jonas Finds Himself on ‘Sunday Best’
item.description: On Nick Jonas' fifth solo album, Sunday Best, he looked inward for inspiration and created what is arguably his strongest music to date.

item.title: Annie Hogan’s ‘Tongues in My Head’ Is Richly Cinematic
item.description: Annie Hogan's exploration of artistic expression shows world-building, all sorts of paintings, mental photographs, and invisible portraits carry great weight.

item.title: Kraftwerk’s Seductive Post-Human
item.description: The power in Kraftwerk's music lies in how they persuade us that the human – sweaty, inefficient, psychologically noisy – is the least necessary component of the future.

item.title: 5 of the Most Unintentionally Terrifying Love Songs
item.description: From Van Halen to Dean Martin, some of the world's most beloved love songs are actually hideously sinister when you dig just below the surface.
